title: Monitoring of psychiatric drugs in nursing homes with capillary blood samples: A feasibility study
summary:
Medicines used to treat mental health conditions (called psychiatric drugs) do not always work well for every person. Some patients may not get enough benefit, while others may experience side effects. That’s why it can be helpful to measure how much of the medicine is in the blood. This helps physicians decide if the dose is right — so that the medicine works well and causes as few side effects as possible.
Normally, venous blood is needed for this — that is, blood taken from a vein, usually from the arm. The blood sample may only be taken by medical staff or by specially trained nursing staff, and only if ordered by a physician.
However, there is a new method: only a small drop of blood is taken from the finger or earlobe. The blood is collected using a small device that absorbs exactly the right amount. This type of blood sampling is less stressful for patients and can also be performed by non-medical staff. As a result, more patients could benefit from having their medication levels measured.

What is the goal of the study?
The study wants to find out whether this new method works well in people living in nursing homes.
To do this, the blood levels of nine psychiatric drugs will be measured in some residents of a nursing home.
The results will help decide whether a larger follow-up study with more participants should be done in the future.

What exactly is being studied?
(1) Whether all the steps and procedures work well
(2) Whether the forms and questionnaires are easy to understand and suitable
(3) Whether the training materials (e.g., for taking blood) are clear and helpful
(4) Whether the lab tests give reliable results
(5) Which measurements are best suited as outcomes for a future larger study

Interventional study:

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
(1) Use of at least one of the following psychiatric drugs:
Citalopram, Clozapine, Desvenlafaxine, Escitalopram, Mirtazapine, Paliperidone, Quetiapine, Risperidone, Venlafaxine, Sertraline

(2) Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Palliative or pre-terminal situation
